title: Nonstop US-Okinawa Flights to Start in 2027
paragraphs: Getting to Okinawa from the United States will soon be much easier. The American airline United Airlines has announced that it will start nonstop flights between San Francisco and Naha, the capital of Okinawa, in 2027.

The first flight will leave San Francisco on March 27, 2027. There will be three flights a week in each direction. Flights from San Francisco will leave on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays at 10:35 a.m. and arrive in Naha at 3:50 p.m. the next day. Flights from Naha will leave on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays. The flights will use Boeing 777-200ER planes. The flight from San Francisco to Okinawa will take about 13 hours and 15 minutes, and the flight back will take about 11 hours.

According to reports, it will be the first regular nonstop flight between the US mainland and Okinawa since 1972. In that year, the US returned Okinawa to Japan after controlling it for 27 years after World War II. At the moment, travelers from the US need to change planes in another city in Asia or in mainland Japan.

The new flights will be useful for tourists, and also for people who want to visit family and friends at the many US military bases in Okinawa. Today, most of Naha's international flights go to other places in Asia, such as Taiwan, South Korea and Singapore.

On the same day, United will also start daily nonstop flights between Los Angeles and Osaka. Tickets for the flights to Okinawa are already on sale, but the route still needs government approval. The flights are planned to run until October 2027.
